rationale: A wins because it sees the bank-side tension B leaves sitting on the table. A's "Plaid needs 12,000 banks to help route payments past the fees banks collect" is a real fourth angle with a different protagonist, outlet universe, and proof burden. B is cleaner in places, but its refusal of "Plaid turns 12,000 bank connections into a payments network" as a duplicate is too timid; that's not a duplicate, that's the distribution fight.
gaps_in_A: "FedNow adoption stories have mostly been about disbursements and B2B" may be true, but it is not in the supplied update. Source it or mark it as context, not fact.
"The prevailing belief in the category is that pay-by-bank is a general-purpose card replacement" is an unsupported premise. Useful angle, sloppy scaffolding.
"The 70% saving only shows up on big-ticket sales" overstates the fact. The update says savings are "up to 70% lower than cards on large transactions," not that smaller transactions never save money.
gaps_in_B: It refuses "Plaid turns 12,000 bank connections into a payments network" as a duplicate. Wrong call. The bank/institution incentive angle is distinct and pitchable if handled carefully.
"which public infrastructure wins" overclaims. One Plaid launch does not prove FedNow is winning anything.
"A flat fee is worse than a percentage on small tickets" assumes the flat fee before Plaid gives it. The breakeven idea is right; the wording gets ahead of the proof.

The next step says the counterposition angle is "the only one that can run on the launch facts alone." Too narrow. The FedNow adoption and breakeven-analysis angles can run too, if the missing technical and pricing proof is supplied.
